diff --git a/solution.cu b/solution.cu
index 3f94d1a..3f7f780 100644
--- a/solution.cu
+++ b/solution.cu
@@ -2,16 +2,15 @@
 #include <cuda_runtime.h>
 
 /*
- * Naive matrix transpose with shared memory (baseline - has severe bank conflicts).
+ * Optimized matrix transpose with padded shared memory to avoid bank conflicts.
  *
- * Performance bottleneck:
- * - Uses shared memory but has severe bank conflicts on write
- * - When threads write to shared memory in column-major order,
- *   all threads in a warp access the same bank, causing 32-way serialization
+ * Performance optimization:
+ * - Uses shared memory with padding to eliminate bank conflicts
+ * - Padding shifts each row by one element, changing bank mapping
+ * - This allows all threads in a warp to access different banks simultaneously
  *
  * This implementation loads a tile into shared memory (coalesced),
- * but then writes it out with bank conflicts, making it slower than
- * an optimized version with padding.
+ * and writes it out with no bank conflicts thanks to the padding.
  */
 
 #define TILE_DIM 32
@@ -19,8 +18,8 @@
 __global__ void k_transpose(const float* __restrict__ input,
                            float* __restrict__ output,
                            int N) {
-    // Shared memory tile (no padding - causes bank conflicts)
-    __shared__ float tile[TILE_DIM][TILE_DIM];
+    // Shared memory tile with padding to avoid bank conflicts
+    __shared__ float tile[TILE_DIM][TILE_DIM + 1];
 
     int x = blockIdx.x * TILE_DIM + threadIdx.x;
     int y = blockIdx.y * TILE_DIM + threadIdx.y;
@@ -38,10 +37,8 @@ __global__ void k_transpose(const float* __restrict__ input,
     int ty = blockIdx.x * TILE_DIM + threadIdx.y;
 
     if (tx < N && ty < N) {
-        // This access has bank conflicts!
-        // threadIdx.x varies across the warp, so tile[threadIdx.x][threadIdx.y]
-        // causes all threads to access different rows with the same column index,
-        // mapping to the same bank
+        // With padding, this access now has no bank conflicts
+        // The +1 padding shifts each row, so threads access different banks
         output[ty * N + tx] = tile[threadIdx.x][threadIdx.y];
     }
 }
